title: Drinking to forget, being fired for quitting, Vine Street
summary: He recalls his wet and dry seasons and the day O'Day fired a pianist for quitting drinking.

story.theme_name: Drink, drugs and the bandstand's casualties
story.community_name: Drugs and drink on the bandstand and the road

blocks.x: How come?
Well I drank to forget.
But it must take a lot of self control to just like —
You’ve got to say what do you want to forget?
What do you want to forget? Okay.
That I’m ashamed.
Uh huh. Ashamed of?

The fact that I drink. That was actually from “The Little Prince.” When he went to see the tippler. He said, “why do you drink so much?” He says, I drink because I’m — whatever it was, “I drink to forget.” “Forget what?” “Forget that I’m ashamed.” “You’re ashamed of what?” “That I drink.” So it’s a round robin. But one time, I’m not going to mention any names again but we had a piano player who was a pretty good drinker at the time. And he really needed to quit drinking. And he quit drinking. So I meet her — we arrive in, I think it was Torino, Italy, and he’s not with the band. She hired somebody else. She didn’t hire him for this tour because of the drinking. But it’s not because he drank too much. So we’re checking in the hotel. We came on different flights but for some reason we’re checking in the hotel. So Anita — I called her Colton, because her real name was Anita Colton. So I always said Colton. So she goes, “Danny, as soon as I take my bags up I’ll meet you in the bar.” I said, “Colton, I’m not drinking.” She looked at me and she says, “I fired a piano player because he quit drinking. I’ll see you in the bar.” I said, “okay, I’ll be right down.” I mean can you imagine getting fired off a gig because you quit drinking? I mean that was Colton man. She was just nuts man. And she had been a big junkie too you know. But my dry season ended right then and there.
I see. You had to readjust your calendar.
Yeah I had to readjust.
Did you ever get fired from a gig because you were drinking?
Naa.
That’s amazing.
Nope.
That you would get fired because you weren’t drinking.
Can you imagine getting fired because you quit drinking? Jeez. That was Colton.
“If I’m doing it, you’re doing it.”
Right. “I’ll see you in the bar.” I said, “I’ll be right down.” I didn’t need to get sent home from wherever we were going.
Uh huh. What was she like in the studio?

I was never with her in the studio. I was with her in a live performance at the Vine Street Bar & Grill which was — a lot of recordings were done at Vine Street — Pete Jolly, Bob Mayes, Gordon Briscer was on it, a very nice man. He’s since gone to his reward.
Who was that you mentioned?
Gordon Briscer, the saxophone player.
